svg.title: Outlook connector code map
svg.desc: The connector's main classes and who calls whom. The command line starts the MCP server or the web UI, or signs in. Both surfaces call service classes: Mailbox, Threads, Exports, Files, Writes and Mutations. The service depends only on the MailReader and MailWriter ports in remote/ports.py, implemented by GraphMailReader over Graph and OwsMailWriter over Outlook Web; both send through one Transport, which takes a token from TokenProvider for every request. Mailbox keeps only the folder cache and the account binding in the local Store. AppContext in bootstrap.py builds all of it once per process.
svg.text: Main classes and who calls whom · arrows point to the callee; data comes back along them
__main__.py · main() parses, then calls one handler per command
_mcp → serve_mcp() · _ui → serve_ui() · _auth, _status → TokenProvider directly (sign-in, sign-out, status; no service)
surfaces/web/web_main.py serve_ui() · routes.py: Starlette JSON API + static JS
reads and exports only, no writes
127.0.0.1 only · session token · stops on Ctrl+C or when idle
services() · domain models in, domain models out
service/ · every domain decision; never sees HTTP, MCP, Graph or OWS JSON
list_messages: whole mailbox or per folder
reply: draft → check history → send it
unclear answer → read back, never resent
helpers: cursors.py self-contained cursors · failures.py ExportError · localfiles.py output folders · domain/models.py the one schema · domain/errors.py
remote/ · the only code that knows URLs, Graph/OWS JSON and id formats
port: list · search · get · count · attachments
port: draft · send · send_draft · read · flag · move · delete
one HTTPS client · host allowlist · ≤ 4 requests at once · GETs retried on 429/5xx
writes sent once, never retried · a rejected token (401) is renewed once
auth/tokens.py · TokenProvider · MSAL · DPAPI-encrypted cache · cross-process lock
Built once per process, on first use:
Each layer calls only the one below it.
The service sees only the two ports, so
Graph and Outlook Web stay swappable.
Reads go to Graph (blue), writes to
one Transport, with a token per request.
first-party public clients · no app registration
inbox rules: proven, no tool yet
private API · gap fill for writes
